title: [Advisory] Ruby: Multiple Memory-Safety Flaws Potentially Enabling RCE
content:
##### SEVERITY AND IMPACT:
- Successful exploitation could eventually allow remote attackers who can supply crafted regex patterns or strings to an application to corrupt heap memory, execute arbitrary code, leak memory contents or crash the process.

- **Current exploitation status**: Proof of Concepts will become available in a week.

##### AFFECTED PRODUCTS:
- Ruby (ruby-lang), the interpreter itself, including end-of-life branches that will not receive fixes
- Applications built on Ruby. Rails and classic-style Sinatra are exposed by default to the case-conversion overflow (GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5).
- Self-hosted software that bundles affected Ruby builds, for example GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, Mastodon, OpenProject, Discourse and Chatwoot

For specific versions, please check the references.

##### VULNERABILITY DETAILS:
- **Prerequisites:**
    - **Regex flaws:** An attacker-controlled regular expression that the application compiles, executes or converts back to text with `Regexp#to_s`.
    - **Case-conversion flaws:** Crafted strings passed to `upcase`, `swapcase`, `downcase(:fold)` or `casecmp?`. One flaw requires single-byte encodings such as ISO-8859-1 or Windows-1252.
    - **Moderate flaw:** A crafted subject string matched against a fixed pattern that uses a case-insensitive backreference.
- **Impact Details:**
    - **Critical:** A one-byte heap overflow in single-byte case conversion (GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5). It is caused by upcasing the "ß" character and has existed since Ruby 2.4.0.
    - **Critical:** A double free in character-class intersection compilation (GHSA-7x2q-68qv-6p8x).
    - **Critical:** A heap overflow from a regex size overflow during compilation (GHSA-3p8q-wmhx-vm2w).
    - **High:** A heap overflow on case-conversion output larger than 4 GiB (GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px).
    - **High:** A heap overflow in `Regexp#to_s` (GHSA-7whj-cfh7-xgm4).
    - **High:** An out-of-bounds read with attacker-controlled memory corruption during case-insensitive matching (GHSA-wpqw-5qxg-m68r).
    - **Moderate:** An out-of-bounds read that may disclose memory or crash the process (GHSA-pvgc-g7gj-pv6h).
- **Available Mitigations:**
    - Vendor patches are available for all supported Ruby branches. End-of-life branches will not be fixed, so migrate them to a supported line.
    - Update the Ruby interpreter itself, then restart application servers and workers and rebuild container images. Updating gems or frameworks alone does not fix the flaws.
    - For bundled self-hosted products, install the vendor's fixed release.
    - CVE IDs have been requested but not yet assigned. Track the flaws through their GHSA IDs in scanners and inventories.
    - **Temporary:**
        - Avoid building or compiling regular expressions from untrusted input.
        - Avoid applying case conversion to untrusted strings in legacy single-byte encodings. For the GHSA-34m4 flaw, converting input to UTF-8 avoids the vulnerable code path.

##### REFERENCES:
Primary:
- Source Advisory: https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2026/11/18/multiple-vulnerabilities-in-regexp-and-string/ (Official Ruby security announcement)
- Vendor Advisory: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5 (Single-byte encoding case-conversion heap overflow)
- Vendor Advisory: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-7x2q-68qv-6p8x (Regex character-class intersection double free)
- Vendor Advisory: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-3p8q-wmhx-vm2w (Regex compile size overflow)
- Vendor Advisory: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-87fm-7w84-j2px (Case-conversion heap overflow above 4 GiB)
- Vendor Advisory: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-7whj-cfh7-xgm4 (Regexp#to_s heap overflow)
- Vendor Advisory: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-wpqw-5qxg-m68r (Case-insensitive match out-of-bounds read)
- Vendor Advisory: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/security/advisories/GHSA-pvgc-g7gj-pv6h (Case-insensitive backreference out-of-bounds read)

Supporting:
- Technical Analysis: https://verialabs.com/ruby2shell/ (Veria Labs "Ruby2Shell" write-up of GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5)
    - Contains root-cause code analysis, details of the overflow primitive, framework exposure and bundled-software status.
    - The authors plan to publish a PoC one week after disclosure.
- Patch Information: https://github.com/ruby/ruby/commit/d582f8f13d700d8e39714d3a8f11eb4bd2bc69f0 (Upstream fix commit for GHSA-34m4-m9fh-gqp5)
- Additional Sources: https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/ruby-fixes-three-regex-engine-bugs.html (Related October Ruby regex engine fixes that were linked to GitLab flaws)
- News Coverage: https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/ruby-releases-fixes-for-7-regex-and.html (The Hacker News report on the seven flaws)

*Timestamp of the Information: 19.11.2026, 11:22*
summary: Ruby's maintainers have disclosed seven memory-safety vulnerabilities in the Ruby interpreter's regular expression engine and string case-conversion code. Five of the flaws have proof-of-concept exploits that achieve remote code execution through crafted patterns or strings. Because the bugs are in the interpreter itself, every application running an affected Ruby version is impacted, and exposure depends on how the application handles untrusted input.
